text:
sam: Quick thread : Sales wants a neat product to sell commit-linked QoS lanes (priority routing + small reservation) for enterprise customers. Need product + contract guardrails.

mira: Important to separate 'priority' from 'guarantee'. Priority lane should bias routing but not promise latency unless SLA addendum.

lina_sales: Customers like the simplicity: buy Commit Tier A -> gets priority lane + 20% reserved capacity on dedicated pool. They expect it to always win routing.

frank_ops: Ops concerns: reserved capacity leads to cold spots if underused; routing bias can starve best-effort customers if not capped. Need enforcement knobs: reserve_pct, soft_reserve_decay, emergency_reclaim.

vivek_fin: Pricing note: commit-linked lanes should be priced as a bundle: commit discount + QoS addon fee. Need clear invoice lines and revenue recognition rules.

legal_rita: Contract perspective: avoid wording like "guaranteed latency". Use "priority routing and reserved capacity subject to pool health and emergency reclaim." Include approval path for bespoke guarantees.

mira: Product config sketch (dev):

```yaml
commit_qos_lane:
  id: commit_qos_v1
  enabled_by_commit: true
  tiers:
    - name: tierA
      commit_usd_min: 50000
      reserved_pct: 0.20
      priority_weight: 1.5
      max_reserve_per_region: 20000
    - name: tierB
      commit_usd_min: 20000
      reserved_pct: 0.10
      priority_weight: 1.2
  soft_reserve_decay_days: 7
  emergency_reclaim_policy:
    allowed: true
    approval_required: true
```

frank_ops: Enforcement plan: router applies `priority_weight` to route scoring; serving layer enforces reserved_pct when pool utilization > 70% (safety threshold). Soft_reserve_decay reduces reserved units over idle period to avoid long-term cold spots.

lina_sales: For the contract, propose two commercial flavors: "Standard Commit QoS" (priority + soft reserve, refundable credits none) and "Committed SLA" (explicit latency SLO, priced separately, requires VP legal sign-off).

legal_rita: Contract snippet suggestion: "Commit QoS Lanes provide priority routing and a best-effort reserved capacity subject to system health. They do not constitute a latency or uptime guarantee unless a separate SLA addendum is executed. Redwood reserves the right to reclaim reserved capacity in emergency events with prior notice where feasible."

vivek_fin: Finance asks: when customers drop commit early, how to handle reserved capacity refunds? Suggest: commit refunds follow existing commit termination rules; reserved capacity is a usage construct and not refundable. Capture in the SOW.

sam: Launch gating checklist idea:
 - API + SDK flags to opt-in/out for qos_lane routing
 - Console shows reserved units, utilization, and soft_reserve_decay status
 - Alerts when reserved consumption >60% and when pool pressure >80%
 - Emergency reclaim workflow + customer notification template
 - Contract language + pricing page copy approved by Legal & Finance
 - Billing lines for commit + qos add-on visible on invoice preview

mira: Edge cases to call out: multi-region customers (how reserve splits), dedicated pool vs shared pool semantics, and interactions with prepaid slabs/credits. We'll need test cases for each.

frank_ops: Implementation notes: add `qos_reserve_id` billing tag propagation so we can attribute usage; create a reclaim endpoint: `POST /admin/reclaim?qos_reserve_id=...&reason=...`. Runbook for SRE oncall to execute reclaim.

infra-bot: Created ticket PROD-5099: implement commit_qos_lane routing weight, reserve enforcement, console UI, and reclaim endpoint (owner=frank_ops, due=2025-06-15).

lina_sales: Commercial workflow: sales must attach a commit SOW with `reserve_pct` and `soft_decay_days` fields. For any SLA requests escalate: AE -> Sales Director -> Legal -> VP.

vivek_fin: Also require invoice preview and explicit acceptance checkbox in purchase flow to prevent billing disputes.

sam: Can we add a conservative default: reserved_pct capped at 25% of pool per customer and a global cap of 30% of pooled capacity so we don't oversubscribe?

mira: Agree on caps. Default: per-customer max 25% reserved of a region pool; global reserved aggregate cap 30% of pool. We'll make these enforceable knobs.

legal_rita: Also insist on an audit trail field `qos_approval_path` in SOWs for any bespoke increases beyond defaults.

frank_ops: Ops to add telemetry: reserve hit rate, wasted reserved units (idle), and reclaim events. We'll feed this into capacity planning.

mira: I'll draft the product spec, the SOW template snippet, and a short marketing blurb that avoids guarantees. Target: draft by Friday COB.

sam: Thanks everyone. Lina, Vivek, please review the draft when ready and sign off.

infra-bot: PROD-5099 updated: added fields qos_approval_path_required=true, per_customer_max_pct=0.25, global_reserved_cap_pct=0.30.

lina_sales: Will review. Quick +1 on the approval path.

mira: Pinging Legal & Finance for final language. We'll lock policy after approvals.
